CheckTitle: Users holding Tier 0 privileged roles are not stale
Description: Each user holding a **Tier 0** privileged directory role is checked against their last **interactive sign-in** from Microsoft Graph `signInActivity`. An account is stale when its last sign-in is older than the configured threshold (default **90 days**), or when it has never signed in. Accounts holding a Tier 0 role through **PIM eligibility** are included when the optional permission is granted.
Notes: Sign-in activity requires the AuditLog.Read.All permission and an Entra ID P1 (or later) licence; when it cannot be read the check reports MANUAL instead of guessing. PIM-eligible Tier 0 holders are included only when the optional RoleEligibilitySchedule.Read.Directory permission is granted. The stale threshold is configurable via stale_privileged_account_days (default 90).

Code.Other: 1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center and open **Identity > Users > All users**. 2. Open the stale account, then select **Revoke sessions** and **Delete** or **Disable** the account after confirming it is no longer needed. 3. Review **Identity > Roles & admins > All roles** and remove the stale account's role assignments. 4. Set up an **Entra access review** on the affected Tier 0 role so dormant access is re-certified regularly.

Recommendation.Text: Investigate why the account is stale. If the user no longer needs the role, remove their Tier 0 role assignments and disable or delete the account, then revoke its sessions. If the user still needs access, confirm the account is in use and protected by strong authentication. Use Entra access reviews to re-certify privileged role holders regularly.

Risk: Stale privileged accounts are rarely monitored but keep their full administrative power, making them an **attractive target** for attackers and a common **leftover after role changes or offboarding**. An attacker who compromises a dormant Tier 0 account gains the highest level of directory access with little chance of being noticed.
